sites.rationale: PMC12229354 reports a Myc-tag inserted into the 'extracellular region' of wild-type human A1R, confirmed at the cell surface by flow cytometry. The paper does not name which extracellular loop or residue carries the tag; no junction residue can be read from the ledger. Reported as a region-level site (insert_after_residue=null). The experiment uses Flag-tagged CAR simultaneously, suggesting the Myc-tag is not at the N-terminus (which would conflict with a Flag-tag in the same assay), but this is inference and not used to pin a residue. Ranked below the N-terminal FLAG site because the position is unresolved and no functional assay of A1R signaling was reported. Short Myc-tag engineered onto the 'extracellular region' of wild-type human A1 receptor expressed on CAR T cells; surface expression confirmed by flow cytometry detecting co-expressed Flag-CAR and Myc-A1R simultaneously. The paper does not name a specific loop or residue junction. [validation: surface_only; position: inferred; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sites.rationale: ADORA1 has no signal peptide: the topology assigns residues 1–9 as extracellular (O), not signal (S). An N-terminal tag therefore prepends before residue 1 (insert_after_residue=0), placing it entirely in the extracellular space with 9 residues of buffer before TM1 begins at residue 10. PMC7116137 explicitly names an 'N-terminal FLAG epitope' on the human A1 receptor and confirms surface delivery by flow cytometry; the same FLAG-tagged construct is used as the wild-type functional control in BRET assays measuring G-protein coupling, establishing both surface expression and functional integrity. PMC4513639 independently reports N-terminal FLAG and SF-TAP tag addition to the same receptor. Python confirms: residue_after = seq[0] = 'M'; residue_before = '' (prepend). No signal peptide cleavage risk. Distance from tag insertion point to TM1 boundary: 9 residues of extracellular sequence. Human A1 receptor with N-terminal FLAG epitope expressed in HEK293 cells; surface delivery confirmed by flow cytometry; FLAG-tagged receptor used as functional control in paired BRET experiments comparing WT vs G279S mutant G-protein coupling. A second paper (PMC4513639) independently confirms N-terminal FLAG and SF-TAP tag addition at the N-terminus of the same receptor. [validation: surface_and_function; position: inferred; source: paper; cited_tag_residue: 0; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: The plasmids encoding the human adenosine A 1 -receptor harboring an N-terminal FLAG epitope, the human dopamine D 1 -receptor harboring an N-terminal HA-epitope, and NanoLuc luciferase (PNL1.1) were obtained from Sinobiological (Beijing, China), from the cDNA resource center (Bloomsburg University), and from Promega (Fitchburg, WI), respectively.

literature_notes: C-terminal eYFP fusion (PMC7116137, PMC4513639): the C-terminus of ADORA1 is intracellular (residues 291–326, topology INTRACELLULAR); this tag does not qualify as an extracellular site and was excluded. YFP-tagged A1R in PMC4513639 (Y288A mutant studies): the YFP position is not stated in the ledger clips and is almost certainly C-terminal (intracellular) given the experimental context (glycosylation/membrane studies); excluded. G279S mutagenesis (PMC7116137): this is a TM7 residue (position 279 falls within TM7, residues 268–290); it is a point mutation study, not a tag insertion, and does not qualify. ECL3 (residues 257–267) contains two cysteines (C260, C263) that likely form a disulfide; no ledger line supports a tag insertion there. ECL1 (69–81) and ECL2 (147–179) have no ledger support for tag insertions in ADORA1 specifically. The SF-TAP tag (PMC4513639) is also N-terminal and corroborates the same site as the FLAG tag; it is not reported as a separate site because it maps to the same junction (insert_after_residue=0).
